LESSON: FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FILLING FORMS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Functional Writing: Filling Forms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Functional Writing: Filling Forms, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we fill forms?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify parts of a simple form for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Functional Writing: Filling Forms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a form related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Functional Writing: Filling Forms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate value of forms for giving information.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Functional Writing: Filling Forms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify parts of a simple form for information,

   Functional Writing: Filling Forms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. create a form related to the theme,

   Functional Writing: Filling Forms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate value of forms for giving information.

   Functional Writing: Filling Forms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to collect a variety of forms and organise them in a portfolio,

2. discuss the parts of a simple form,

3. work collaboratively to create a form seeking for basic information from peers like name, school, favorite subject, class, favourite cultural food,

4. share the forms with their friends for filling,

5. provide information in the forms as per instructions given,

6. work jointly to create digital forms in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to collect a variety of forms and organise them in a portfolio,
2. discuss the parts of a simple form,
3. work collaboratively to create a form seeking for basic information from peers like name, school, favorite subject, class, favourite cultural food,
4. share the forms with their friends for filling,
5. provide information in the forms as per instructions given,
6. work jointly to create digital forms in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Functional Writing: Filling Forms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when creating forms using

digital devices.

• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner effectively orders and prioritises tasks when looking for forms and organises

them in a portfolio.

48

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner works harmoniously with peers to create forms.

• Integrity: This is promoted as learner displays transparency when filling sample forms related to the theme as per the

instructions given.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner uses digital devices to create a variety of forms.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of filling forms to their learning of functional writing in Kiswahili and English.
